questions.stem: Why must a medical tracer isotope have a short half-life?

options.text: So it decays quickly and does not remain radioactive in the patient for long
So it is cheaper to produce
So it can be detected more easily

questions.explanation: A short half-life ensures the tracer decays quickly after the medical procedure, minimising the patient's radiation dose. However, the half-life must be long enough for the procedure to be completed. Technetium-99m, with a half-life of 6 hours, is ideal for many diagnostic procedures.

questions.stem: Alpha radiation is used in smoke detectors. What happens when smoke enters the detector?

options.text: The smoke reflects the alpha particles back to the source
The smoke absorbs the alpha particles, reducing the ionisation current, triggering the alarm
The smoke increases the ionisation current
The smoke reacts chemically with the alpha particles

questions.explanation: In a smoke detector, alpha particles from americium-241 ionise the air, creating a small electric current. When smoke enters, smoke particles absorb the alpha particles (which have very low penetrating power), reducing the ionisation current. This drop in current triggers the alarm.
